results.title: which leads to the rise of sequential recommendations. Sequential recommenders based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) (Tang and Wang, 2018), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) (Hidasi et al., 2016), and self-attention (Sun et al., 2019; Zhang et al., 2019; Kang and McAuley, 2018; Zhou et al., 2020; Rajput et al., 2023) have become prevalent in the era of deep learning. Notably, leveraging a T5-like backbone, Rajput et al. 2023 formalize recommendation as generative retrieval, i.e., autoregressively decode the identifiers of the target items, and achieve the current SOTA. While structurally resembling LLMs, it lacks their pre-training knowledge and the accompanying natural language reasoning potential. Our proposed approach adopts self-attention for sequential recommendation, specifically harnessing LLMs as backbones. We compare against various baselines from all the classes discussed above.

item.text: {"text":"Search found related 2023–2026 work, but no verified exact match combining GRU4Rec, a lightweight text encoder trained from scratch, and semantic hard negatives. Recent text-aware methods largely depend on pretrained models: [CLA-Rec (ICDM 2024)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10884256/) aligns LLM-derived description embeddings with collaborative information, then uses a Transformer; [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) encodes titles, descriptions and reviews with BERT. These support investigating recommendation-specific text alignment, but their architectures, pretrained weights and review inputs do not satisfy this task’s constraints.\n\nA constraint-compatible experimental hypothesis: retain one GRU4Rec network per category; encode available titles/descriptions using randomly initialized token embeddings plus masked mean pooling or a small CNN; jointly learn a gated combination with item-ID embeddings through next-item prediction. Apply the same item representation to history inputs and candidate scoring. Optionally add a low-weight ID–text alignment objective within that network. Mix uniform negatives with moderately difficult candidates selected using the current jointly learned representations, excluding known training positives. Treat text similarity as a sampling cue, not evidence of incompatibility or current need. [Context-Aware Negative Sampling (2025)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/11021640) demonstrates that context-sensitive negative selection can affect sequential recommendation, but reports an accuracy–diversity tradeoff; it does not establish HR@10 gains for semantic negatives. Validate text fusion first, then auxiliary alignment and hard-negative sampling separately under the fixed macro validation protocol."}
